translationRepairs: The imperial edict read: "Among King Wen's ten sons, Kang Shu alone was singled out for honor because he was recognized for his virtue.
The imperial edict read: "Among Kang Shu's ten kinsmen, he alone was singled out for honor because this was to reward virtue.

康叔親屬有十而獨尊者 names Kang Shu's ten kinsmen, not King Wen's sons; the proposal rightly drops the invention, but its after is awkward, so revise to keep the clear among-kinsmen wording and 褒有德也 as rewarding virtue.

In the third month of year 6, day wu-shen first day, day yi-hai, Censor subject Guang acting as Minister of the Imperial Secretariat and Aide Fei, sent the censor memorial, saying: Chancellor subject Qing Que, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang, Grand Master of Ceremonies subject Chong, Grand Herald subject Xi, Crown Prince Junior Tutor subject An acting as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, risking death submit: Grand Marshal Qubing submitted memorial saying: 'Your Majesty has favored me excessively, allowing subject Qubing to await punishment in the ranks of the honored.

In the third month of year 6, day wu-shen first day, day yi-hai, Censor subject Guang acting as Minister of the Imperial Secretariat and Aide Fei, sent the censor memorial, saying: Chancellor subject Qing Di, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang, Grand Master of Ceremonies subject Chong, Grand Herald subject Xi, Crown Prince Junior Tutor subject An acting as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, risking death submit: Grand Marshal Qubing submitted memorial saying: 'Your Majesty has favored me excessively, allowing subject Qubing to await punishment in the ranks of the honored.
丞相臣青翟 is Qing Di; literal Qing Que misreads 翟 and the proposed name fix is exact.
Subjects Qing Que, Tang and others should uphold righteousness and follow duty, foolishly dull and not up to affairs.
Subjects Qing Di, Tang and others should uphold righteousness and follow duty, foolishly dull and not up to affairs.
臣青翟 again requires Qing Di; replacing Qing Que corrects the same romanization error without other changes.

'Chancellor subject Qing Que, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang risking death speak: Subjects respectfully with Marquis subject Ying Qi, central two thousand shi and two thousand shi subject He, Remonstrance Official and Erudite subject An and others discuss: We have heard that Zhou enfeoffed eight hundred, the Ji surname stood together, supporting the Son of Heaven.

'Chancellor subject Qing Di, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang risking death speak: Subjects respectfully with Marquis subject Ying Qi, central two thousand shi and two thousand shi subject He, Remonstrance Official and Erudite subject An and others discuss: We have heard that Zhou enfeoffed eight hundred, the Ji surname stood together, supporting the Son of Heaven.
丞相臣青翟 is Qing Di; the proposed literal correctly replaces Qing Que.
Continues the line of Xiao Wen Zhong at Ju, rewards and encourages ministers like Pingjin Marquis and others.
Continues the line of Xiao Wen Zhong at Zan, rewards and encourages ministers like Pingjin Marquis and others.
於酂 is the place Zan; literal Ju is a toponym error, and Zan matches the Chinese and the idiomatic.

'Chancellor subject Qing Que, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang risking death speak: Subjects Qing Que and others with marquises, officials of two thousand shi, remonstrance officials, erudites subject Qing and others discuss: Risking death memorialize requesting to establish imperial sons as feudal kings.

'Chancellor subject Qing Di, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang risking death speak: Subjects Qing Di and others with marquises, officials of two thousand shi, remonstrance officials, erudites subject Qing and others discuss: Risking death memorialize requesting to establish imperial sons as feudal kings.
Both 丞相臣青翟 and 臣青翟等 are Qing Di; correcting both Qing Que instances is required and accurate.
The imperial edict read: 'Among King Wen's ten sons, Kang Shu alone was singled out for honor because he was recognized for his virtue.
The imperial edict read: 'Among Kang Shu's ten kinsmen, he alone was singled out for honor because he was recognized for his virtue.
康叔親屬有十而獨尊者 does not name King Wen; the proposed among-kinsmen wording restores the Chinese while preserving the rest of the good idiomatic sentence.

Subjects Qing Que, Tang, Erudite subject Jiang Xing and others have heard that Kang Shu had ten relatives, King Wu succeeded to the throne, Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, eight of them were established as great states by the honor of their ancestors.

Subjects Qing Di, Tang, Erudite subject Jiang Xing and others have heard that Kang Shu had ten relatives, King Wu succeeded to the throne, Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, eight of them were established as great states by the honor of their ancestors.
臣青翟 is Qing Di; the single Qing Que→Qing Di fix is correct.

Now feudal lords' branch sons are enfeoffed as feudal kings, yet to make imperial sons marquises, subjects Qing Que, Tang and others secretly and prostrate consider it, all think noble and base lose order, causing the world to lose hope, cannot.

Now feudal lords' branch sons are enfeoffed as feudal kings, yet to make imperial sons marquises, subjects Qing Di, Tang and others secretly and prostrate consider it, all think noble and base lose order, causing the world to lose hope, cannot.
臣青翟、臣湯等 requires Qing Di; the proposed replacement is exact.

"The Chancellor Qing Di, the Grand Coachman He, the Grand Master of Ceremonies Chong acting as Grandee Secretary, and the Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince An acting as Director of the Imperial Clan, at the risk of death state: We, your servants Qing Di and the others, previously submitted a memorial regarding the Grand Marshal Qubing's petition stating that the imperial princes have not yet been granted titles. We respectfully, together with the Grandee Secretary Tang, the officials of the central two-thousand-shi and two-thousand-shi ranks, the Remonstrant Officials, and the Erudites including Qing, at the risk of death requested that the imperial princes Hong and the others be established as feudal kings.

"The Chancellor Qing Di, the Grand Coachman He, the Grand Master of Ceremonies Chong acting as Grandee Secretary, and An, the Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, acting as Director of the Imperial Clan, at the risk of death state: We, your servants Qing Di and the others, previously submitted a memorial regarding the Grand Marshal Qubing's petition stating that the imperial princes have not yet been granted titles. We respectfully, together with the Grandee Secretary Tang, the officials of the central two-thousand-shi and two-thousand-shi ranks, the Remonstrant Officials, and the Erudites including Qing, at the risk of death requested that the imperial princes Hong and the others be established as feudal kings.
太子少傅臣安 makes An the Junior Tutor, not a Crown Prince; the reordered English removes the false Crown Prince An reading while keeping titles and the rest intact.

'Chancellor subject Qing Que, Grand Coachman subject He, acting as Censor-in-Chief Grand Master of Ceremonies subject Chong, Crown Prince Junior Tutor subject An acting as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan risking death speak: Subjects Qing Que and others previously memorialized Grand Marshal subject Qubing submitted memorial saying imperial sons have no titles, subjects respectfully with Censor-in-Chief subject Tang, central two thousand shi, two thousand shi, remonstrance officials, erudites subject Qing and others risking death request to establish imperial sons subject Hong and others as feudal kings.

'Chancellor subject Qing Di, Grand Coachman subject He, acting as Censor-in-Chief Grand Master of Ceremonies subject Chong, Crown Prince Junior Tutor subject An acting as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan risking death speak: Subjects Qing Di and others previously memorialized Grand Marshal subject Qubing submitted memorial saying imperial sons have no titles, subjects respectfully with Censor-in-Chief subject Tang, central two thousand shi, two thousand shi, remonstrance officials, erudites subject Qing and others risking death request to establish imperial sons subject Hong and others as feudal kings.
丞相臣青翟 and 臣青翟等 are Qing Di; both literal Qing Que forms must be corrected.
Subjects Qing Que and others secretly with Marquis subject Shou Cheng and twenty-seven others discuss; all said this violates the proper order of high and low.
Subjects Qing Di and others secretly with Marquis subject Shou Cheng and twenty-seven others discuss; all said this violates the proper order of high and low.
臣青翟等 is Qing Di; Qing Que is the same romanization error.
The Xiongnu are cruel and beastly by nature, invading and plundering as bandits and thieves, and moreover they deal treacherously with the border settlements.
The Xiongnu are cruel to the aged and beast-hearted, invading and plundering as bandits and thieves, and moreover they deal treacherously with the border settlements.
虐老獸心 specifies cruelty to the aged plus a beast-like heart; dropping 虐老 into generic beastliness omits that element, and the proposed wording restores it.
I commanded generals to go punish their crimes, ten thousand man leaders, thousand man leaders, thirty-two lords all came, surrendered and fled the army.
I commanded generals to go punish their crimes; ten-thousand-man leaders, thousand-man leaders, and thirty-two lords all came, surrendering at the appointed time and fleeing to our forces.
降期奔師 is surrendering at the appointed time and fleeing toward (joining) the Han forces, not fleeing the army; the proposed literal matches that sense.
What wise rulers make, certainly not what shallow learners can know, not what broad learning strong memory gentlemen cannot thoroughly understand the intent.
What a wise ruler makes is certainly not something shallow learners can know; it is not something that gentlemen of broad learning and strong memory cannot thoroughly fathom in its intent.
非淺聞者所能知，非博聞彊記君子者所不能究竟其意 is a double negation that the original literal garbles; the proposed wording restores grammatical English and the Chinese sense.
he admonished the King of Yan not to stir up resentment and not to turn from virtue;
he admonished the King of Yan not to stir up resentment and not to cultivate virtue;
無修德 is a prohibition parallel to 無作怨; "not to turn from virtue" reverses 無, and "not to cultivate virtue" follows the Chinese as written.
warned the King of Yan not to create resentment, not to turn from virtue;
warned the King of Yan not to create resentment, not to cultivate virtue;
Same unit: literal 無修德 means do not cultivate virtue, not "not to turn from virtue."
Also saying 'ministers do not create awe' means do not let them because of lightness double righteousness.
Also saying 'ministers do not create awe' means do not let them because of lightness betray righteousness.
倍義 is betray righteousness, not double it; the proposal's brackets add an interpretive gloss not in the Chinese, so revise to the betrayal fix alone.
Now land and townships increasingly few, I wish to together with King Xu of Guangling raise troops.
Now land and townships increasingly few, I wish to together with the King of Guangling raise troops.
與廣陵王共發兵 names only the King of Guangling; inserting personal name Xu is unsupported in this unit.
Establish King Xu of Guangling as supreme, I again rule Chu 32 cities, like King Yuan time.'
Establish the King of Guangling as supreme, I again rule Chu 32 cities, like King Yuan time.'
［立］廣陵王為上 likewise has only the title King of Guangling; the invented Xu must be removed.
'Do not pity virtue' means do not let king turn back on virtue.
'Do not go against virtue' means do not let the king turn back on virtue.
無俷德 uses 俷 "go against/violate," not pity; the proposed gloss matches the commentary sense 勿使王背德.
